- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.5.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling beyond 10% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price change.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3) and price is near 75–85, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment median as anchor for correction.
